 Trae Young 
 WAS 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Player Stats

 The Washington Wizards will start Trae Young, Kyshawn George, AJ Dybantsa, Alex Sarr, and Deandre Ayton against Hawks on Friday. 
 Anthony Davis is out with an ankle injury, so instead of starting Bilal Coulibaly who started in Dybantsa’s absence, the Wizards have elected to start Ayton at center. This is part of the reason they brought him in last summer, so if he’s available in a redraft league, he could be worth a stream. 
 -  Brian Taylor

 Anthony Davis 
 WAS 
 Forward-Center 
 #23 
 Personalize your Rotoworld feed by favoriting players 
 Anthony Davis (ankle) is out for Friday’s game against the Hawks. 
 Davis will miss Friday’s game with a sprained right ankle. Whether he moves into the starting lineup or comes off the bench, Deandre Ayton is likely to see his playing time increase. 
 Anthony Davis 
 WAS 
 Forward-Center 
 #23 
 Anthony Davis (ankle) is questionable to play against the Hawks on Friday. 
 Davis tweaked his ankle in the first quarter against Atlanta on Wednesday, but he was able to play through it and ended up having a strong night. If he isn’t able to suit up in Friday’s rematch, Deandre Ayton would likely slide into the starting unit. 
 AJ Dybantsa 
 WAS 
 Forward 
 #4 
 AJ Dybantsa had 9 points (4-of-12 FGs, 1-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, and three assists on Wednesday. 
 The Hawks clearly bothered him with their physicality where he missed several buckets around the rim. A lot of his recent value was coming from shooting 93% at the free throw line and he shot 1-of-4 in this game. He will have better performances than this and once he gets used to more of the NBA physicality, he’s going to be a really good player. His athleticism and size allow him to do things that very few players in the league can do. 
 Kyshawn George 
 WAS 
 Forward 
 #18 
 Kyshawn George with a monster 25 points (10-of-14 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), four rebounds, seven assists, and three 3-pointers in the 120-105 loss to the Hawks. 
 Kyshawn has fit right into his role in the starting lineup and has been a very impactful and important player on this Wizards team. He impacts winning, doesn’t do more than is required, and will do whatever the team asks him to do. He was one of the only players on the Wizards that could hit 3’s in this game with the team going 6-of-26 from three (23.1%). 
 Anthony Davis 
 WAS 
 Forward-Center 
 #23 
 Anthony Davis took advantage of the Hawks’ size with 26 points (12-of-19 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 10 rebounds, three assists and three blocks in a loss. 
 He did tweak his ankle in the first quarter which will be something to monitor if it flares up but it didn’t impact him much in this game. He took advantage of his size over the Hawk’s smaller big men and had a good game. The next game the Wizards play is against the Hawks in Atlanta, so if he’s healthy, it’s possible that he has a similar performance against them on Friday. 
 Alex Sarr 
 WAS 
 Center 
 #20 
 Alex Sarr (knee) and Bilal Coulibaly (illness) are available for Wednesday’s game against the Hawks. 
 Sarr and Coulibaly are available after being listed as questionable on earlier injury reports. The former will fill his usual role as the starting center, while the latter will provide wing depth off the bench. 
 Alex Sarr 
 WAS 
 Center 
 #20 
 Alex Sarr (knee) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Hawks. 
 Sarr did not play in Monday’s win over the Magic, with Deandre Ayton moving into the starting lineup and playing 24 minutes. He should take on a similar workload if Sarr remains out on Wednesday. 
 AJ Dybantsa 
 WAS 
 Forward 
 #4 
 AJ Dybantsa had 21 points (7-of-17 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, two assists, three steals and one three-pointer against the Magic on Monday. 
 Dybantsa has now scored at least 17 points in the first three games of his career. He also recorded three steals on Monday and has four steals total over his last two games. Dybantsa’s minutes have increased from 27 to 30 to 33 in his first three games. While his offensive game continues to round into form, he could be a difference-maker on the defensive end given his penchant for steals. 
 Anthony Davis 
 WAS 
 Forward-Center 
 #23 
 Anthony Davis had 27 points (12-of-17 FGs, 2-of-2 FTS), nine rebounds, one assist, three steals and one three-pointer in the Wizards’ 103-94 victory over the Magic on Monday. 
 Davis has now scored at least 25 points and at least nine rebounds in three of his last four games. The 33-year-old center had played in 71 games in the previous three seasons entering this year, but his production has been solid. While Davis’ injury history casts doubt over his durability going forward, he’s been a big part of the Wizards going 4-3 in the early part of the season. 
 Deandre Ayton 
 WAS 
 Center 
 #8 
 Trae Young, Kyshawn George, AJ Dybantsa, Anthony Davis and Deandre Ayton will start against the Magic on Monday. 
 With Alex Sarr (ankle) sidelined, Ayton will get the starting nod at center. Ayton hasn’t been productive as a reserve this season, though this starting opportunity should allow him to have a solid outing.

 Tre Johnson scored 23 points (9-of-16 FGs), a rebound, an assist, and five 3-pointers in 27 minutes off the bench. 
 Tre Johnson took a lot of the usage vacated by Anthony Davis (ankle) in this game and hit several 3’s. His fantasy game is very empty outside of the scoring and 3’s which limits his fantasy upside, but he is a really good shooter. If AD misses another game, you can consider a stream of Tre Johnson if you’re in need of the points and 3’s. He’s much better in points leagues than category leagues.
 -  Brian Taylor

 Onyeka Okongwu with 22 points (8-of-12 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), ten rebounds, an assist, four steals, and two 3-pointers on Friday in win over the Wizards. 
 That’s back-to-back good games for Okongwu who seems to be bouncing back from the tough start. Jalen Johnson (ankle) is still out which has helped Okongwu with shot attempts. There will be some regression wants he comes back, but he should return mid round value for the rest of the season barring injury. If you can pull off a sell high after the past few games, I’d look to see if that is a possibility. 
 -  Brian Taylor

 Luguentz Dort 
 ATL 
 Guard 
 #0 
 Player Stats

 Luguentz Dort put up 25 points (9-of-15 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, two steals, and five 3-pointers on Friday. 
 Dort hasn’t had the same role that he had with Oklahoma City, but it was a good game in this one. He’s having a similar output to last season in terms of efficiency, which isn’t great since he’s been below 40% from the field. He has been impactful on defense and has value there. He’s still a deeper league guy despite having a good performance. He has been notorious for being volatile in terms of his day-to-day performances. He’s worth a stream in start while keeping in mind that he might ruin your FG% category. 
 -  Brian Taylor

 Nickeil Alexander-Walker scored 28 points (7-of-20 FGs, 10-of-10 FTs), two rebounds, two assists, two steals, and four 3-pointers in 139-132 win over the Wizards. 
 Nickeil has improved from last season where he won most improved player. From struggling to be efficient in New Orleans to leading the Hawks in scoring is a great story. While Jalen Johnson is out, Alexander-Walker should continue to put up points in bunches while getting good steals, good 3’s and good free throws while being a high level scorer.

 Naz Reid 
 CHA 
 Center-Forward 
 #0 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Naz Reid tallied 14 points (6-of-17 FGs), six rebounds, two assists and one steal over 26 minutes in a blowout loss to the Celtics on Friday.
 There weren’t a ton of bright spots for the Hornets as they failed to eclipse 91 points for the fourth time in 10 games to open this season. Boston raced out to a massive 70-39 advantage by halftime and never really looked back. Coming off a season-high 28-point effort against the Nets earlier this week, Reid drew the start in place of an injured Moussa Diabaté (quad) in this one and led Charlotte with 17 shot attempts. He’s shown some signs of life recently after a rough start to his Hornets debut.
 -  George Bissell 
 Recap

 Derrick White 
 BOS 
 Guard 
 #9 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Derrick White amassed 18 points (6-of-10 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), four rebounds, five assists and one steal over 25 minutes in a lopsided win over the Hornets on Friday.
 White enjoyed his best shooting performance from beyond the arc in some time, connecting on 4-of-6 attempts after shooting just 29 percent from three-point range through his first eight games. He would’ve notched his second consecutive 20-point effort, but he was able to sit out most of the second half with Boston leading by nearly 40 points. The Celtics close out a four-game week with a road matchup against the Bucks, who White torched for a season-high 24 points earlier this week.
 -  George Bissell 
 Recap 
 More Derrick White News
 Tidjane Salaün 
 CHA 
 Forward 
 #31 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Tidjane Salaün posted 13 points (3-of-11 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs) and four rebounds over 23 minutes in a one-sided defeat at the hands of the Celtics on Friday.
 Salaün did most of his damage in the second half once the outcome was no longer in doubt after replacing an injured Brandon Miller, who left the contest with groin soreness in the second quarter. It wasn’t an inspiring shooting performance, especially since he was just 2-of-8 from three-point range, but he managed to get to the charity stripe a couple times during the blowout. The 21-year-old former lottery pick remains an intriguing talent, but he’s averaging less than 15 minutes for an injury-depleted Charlotte club this season. That could change if Miller winds up requiring an extended absence. He can be safely ignored in all fantasy leagues for the moment.
 -  George Bissell
